Layout title objects

Source: R/zz-gen-layout.R
go_layout_title.Rd

Properties of layout.title.

Usage

go_layout_title(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  automargin = NULL,
  font = NULL,
  pad = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  text = NULL,
  x = NULL,
  xanchor = NULL,
  xref = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  yanchor = NULL,
  yref = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

go_layout_title_font(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  color = NULL,
  family = NULL,
  lineposition = NULL,
  shadow = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  style = NULL,
  textcase = NULL,
  variant = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

go_layout_title_pad(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  b = NULL,
  l = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  t = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

go_layout_title_subtitle(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  font = NULL,
  text = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

go_layout_title_subtitle_font(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  color = NULL,
  family = NULL,
  lineposition = NULL,
  shadow = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  style = NULL,
  textcase = NULL,
  variant = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

arg

Optional named list, or graph object of the same type, to initialise properties from (constructors). Named arguments take precedence.

...

Further properties, including nested properties in "magic underscore" form, e.g. marker_size = 10 for marker = list(size = 10). Property values may be one-sided formulas, evaluated in data for add_*() functions.

automargin

Determines whether the title can automatically push the figure margins. If `yref='paper'` then the margin will expand to ensure that the title doesn't overlap with the edges of the container. If `yref='container'` then the margins will ensure that the title doesn't overlap with the plot area, tick labels, and axis titles. If `automargin=true` and the margins need to be expanded, then y will be set to a default 1 and yanchor will be set to an appropriate default to ensure that minimal margin space is needed. Note that when `yref='paper'`, only 1 or 0 are allowed y values. Invalid values will be reset to the default 1. Logical.

font

go_layout_title(): Sets the title font. Named list or go_layout_title_font() object.

go_layout_title_subtitle(): Sets the subtitle font. Named list or go_layout_title_subtitle_font() object.

pad

Sets the padding of the title. Each padding value only applies when the corresponding `xanchor`/`yanchor` value is set accordingly. E.g. for left padding to take effect, `xanchor` must be set to "left". The same rule applies if `xanchor`/`yanchor` is determined automatically. Padding is muted if the respective anchor value is "middle"/"center". Named list or go_layout_title_pad() object.

subtitle

Named list or go_layout_title_subtitle() object.

text

go_layout_title(): Sets the plot's title. String.

go_layout_title_subtitle(): Sets the plot's subtitle. String.

x

Sets the x position with respect to `xref` in normalized coordinates from 0 (left) to 1 (right). Number in the interval [0, 1].

xanchor

Sets the title's horizontal alignment with respect to its x position. "left" means that the title starts at x, "right" means that the title ends at x and "center" means that the title's center is at x. "auto" divides `xref` by three and calculates the `xanchor` value automatically based on the value of `x`. One of "auto", "left", "center", "right".

xref

Sets the container `x` refers to. "container" spans the entire `width` of the plot. "paper" refers to the width of the plotting area only. One of "container", "paper".

y

Sets the y position with respect to `yref` in normalized coordinates from 0 (bottom) to 1 (top). "auto" places the baseline of the title onto the vertical center of the top margin. Number in the interval [0, 1].

yanchor

Sets the title's vertical alignment with respect to its y position. "top" means that the title's cap line is at y, "bottom" means that the title's baseline is at y and "middle" means that the title's midline is at y. "auto" divides `yref` by three and calculates the `yanchor` value automatically based on the value of `y`. One of "auto", "top", "middle", "bottom".

yref

Sets the container `y` refers to. "container" spans the entire `height` of the plot. "paper" refers to the height of the plotting area only. One of "container", "paper".

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

color

Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

family

HTML font family - the typeface that will be applied by the web browser. The web browser can only apply a font if it is available on the system where it runs. Provide multiple font families, separated by commas, to indicate the order in which to apply fonts if they aren't available. String.

lineposition

Sets the kind of decoration line(s) with text, such as an "under", "over" or "through" as well as combinations e.g. "under+over", etc. Any combination of "under", "over", "through" joined with "+", or one of "none".

shadow

Sets the shape and color of the shadow behind text. "auto" places minimal shadow and applies contrast text font color. See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/text-shadow for additional options. String.

size

Number in the interval [1, Inf].

style

Sets whether a font should be styled with a normal or italic face from its family. One of "normal", "italic".

textcase

Sets capitalization of text. It can be used to make text appear in all-uppercase or all-lowercase, or with each word capitalized. One of "normal", "word caps", "upper", "lower".

variant

Sets the variant of the font. One of "normal", "small-caps", "all-small-caps", "all-petite-caps", "petite-caps", "unicase".

weight

Sets the weight (or boldness) of the font. Integer in the interval [1, 1000].

b

The amount of padding (in px) along the bottom of the component. Number.

l

The amount of padding (in px) on the left side of the component. Number.

r

The amount of padding (in px) on the right side of the component. Number.

t

The amount of padding (in px) along the top of the component. Number.

Value

Each go_*() function returns a graph object of the same class as its name; add_*() functions return the modified figure.

Details

go_layout_title() and the nested object constructors below create validated graph objects (named lists). Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when an object is created or modified (see plotly_obj-modify()).

Nested objects documented here:

go_layout_title_font()

layout.title.font: Sets the title font.

go_layout_title_pad()

layout.title.pad: Sets the padding of the title. Each padding value only applies when the corresponding `xanchor`/`yanchor` value is set accordingly. E.g. for left padding to take effect, `xanchor` must be set to "left". The same rule applies if `xanchor`/`yanchor` is determined automatically. Padding is muted if the respective anchor value is "middle"/"center".

go_layout_title_subtitle()

layout.title.subtitle

go_layout_title_subtitle_font()

layout.title.subtitle.font: Sets the subtitle font.
